open_points.subject: Model M13 — PrincipalPublisher
open_points.text: the acting principal (M07) that published it — Kernel for the agent naming its session, or the owner (R0-88).
open_points.question: When Cabinet Kernel publishes a pointer, is the agent-session identity part of PrincipalPublisher, or does PrincipalPublisher contain only the Kernel principal?
options: The publisher contains both Kernel's principal and the agent-session identity.
The publisher contains only Kernel's principal; the session is stored elsewhere on the pointer.
The publisher contains only Kernel's principal and no session is retained.
open_points.default_guess: Include the agent-session identity in PrincipalPublisher for a Kernel publication.

witness.initial: Two registered agent sessions S1 and S2 can both publish on a project granted to them.
events: Kernel publishes pointer P1 for session S1.
Kernel publishes pointer P2 for session S2.
outcomes: P1 and P2 carry equal PrincipalPublisher values because both name only Kernel.
P1 and P2 carry different PrincipalPublisher values because the session is part of the publisher.
witness.observer: The owner or a trace correlator reading the pointers sees whether their publishing sessions can be distinguished.

open_points.subject: Model M20 — PendingConfirmation
open_points.text: Facts: its one-time value;
open_points.question: Is the pending confirmation's one-time value the same fact as M11's “confirmation id”, or are they two distinct facts?
options: They are the same value, minted by Registry for each confirmation.
They are distinct values and both must be recorded.
Only the confirmation id is recorded; “one-time value” is descriptive wording.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the one-time value and confirmation id as the same Registry-minted value.

open_points.subject: Models M20 and M21 — confirmation binding
open_points.text: the inputs it is bound to, by their digest;
open_points.question: Does a pending import confirmation bind only the uploaded bytes' digest, or does it also bind the UploadedFile upload number so that a later upload of identical bytes is distinguishable?
options: Bind both the digest and upload number.
Bind only the digest, so identical re-uploads remain interchangeable.
open_points.default_guess: Bind both the digest and upload number.

witness.initial: An owner session holds upload 1 with bytes B and digest D, and Registry shows a confirmation bound to that upload.
events: The owner uploads the same bytes B again, creating upload 2 with the same digest D but a different upload number.
The owner submits the confirmation shown for upload 1.
outcomes: The confirmation matches because M20 records its bound inputs only by digest D.
The confirmation does not match because M21 says the upload number makes the confirmation bind the particular upload it showed.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether the import is accepted, and the store shows whether the import was applied.

open_points.subject: Model M21 — UploadedFile
open_points.text: Facts: its bytes, as uploaded; their digest, by which the mapping names the file (A16 rule 2); and its upload number within the session
open_points.question: Who derives the digest and who assigns the upload number, and is the number derived from the sequence of upload events in that owner session?
options: Registry derives the digest from the uploaded bytes and assigns a session-scoped number for each upload event.
The owner supplies either or both values and Registry stores them.
Another component derives or assigns them before Registry receives the upload.
open_points.default_guess: Registry derives the digest from the bytes and assigns a new session-scoped number to every upload event.

open_points.subject: Model M28 — OwnerAuditAction
open_points.text: A row of the owner audit table: which audit action (M09, R0-58) an accepted owner action writes
open_points.question: Does OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS contain rows only for owner actions that create an audit entry, or must every accepted owner action have a row, including reads and other actions that write no audit entry?
options: Only audit-producing owner actions have rows.
Every owner action has a row, with an explicit no-audit value where applicable.
Every accepted owner action writes an audit entry.
open_points.default_guess: Include rows only for owner actions that produce audit entries.

witness.initial: The owner has a valid session and an existing customer.
events: The owner successfully reads the customer.
outcomes: No OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS row is read because the table covers only audit-producing actions and ordinary reads create no audit entry.
Every accepted owner action requires a row, forcing either a no-audit representation not listed among M28's facts or an audit entry for the read.
witness.observer: The owner reading the audit log and the implementation consuming OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS see the difference.
